newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo shares rebound, Bangkok higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo shares rebound, Bangkok higher.

text.p: Tokyo stocks recovered on Wednesday from a sharp fall the previous day as investors sought blue-chip bargains, and Bangkok's bourse was buoyed by local buying in a market hit heavily in the past month, brokers said.
Other major Asian markets were closed for Christmas.
Brokers in Tokyo said the rally, helped by seasonal cheer on Wall Street, lacked vigour.
The market had a full-day trading session, but activity was thinned by the absence of foreign brokers celebrating Christmas.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares rose two percent, regaining much of the ground it had lost on Tuesday on gloom about the Japanese economy.

The Nikkei closed up 387.70 points or 2.02 percent at 19,549.41. The index fell 528.75 points or 2.69 percent on Tuesday to a 12-month low of 19,161.71, depressed by concerns about the impact of fiscal tightening next year on Japan's fledgling economic recovery.
With volume light, Wall Street's Christmas Eve rally to a near-record closing high overnight helped lift the market early on, brokers said.

Stocks have taken a battering since the government confirmed last week that it will raise Japan's consumption tax next April and end special income tax cuts as part of a drive to rein in government borrowing.
Thai stocks rallied to close higher for the third consecutive day, gaining 1.78 percent on local bargain hunting and window dressing of year-end corporate balance sheets, brokers said.
The SET index rose 14.70 points to 841.42 on thin turnover.
"The index rose purely on local speculation and buying by some listed firms seeking to window dress year-end balance sheets," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
Shanghai's B share index ended slightly down on Wednesday mainly due to a fall in a real estate developer, traders said.
Trading was dull and dominated by local retail investors, with foreign investors taking a Christmas holiday, they said.
The index fell 0.289 points, or 0.45 percent, to 64.299 on thin volume of 7.7 million shares worth $3.5 million.
The dollar was firmer in late Tokyo trade at 114.65/70 yen and 1.5570/80 marks, against New York's Tuesday close of 114.43/48 yen and 1.5554/64 marks.
In Tokyo, gold bullion closed at $368.60/369.10, against $368.90/369.40 in New York on Tuesday.
SIMEX Brent oil trading will resume on Friday.
